literal: Strangers' fault like, one's own fault if able to see, evil is there [question] for enduring life?
translation: If people could see their own faults just as they see the faults of others, would any harm ever come to their enduring lives?
modern: மற்றவர்களுடைய குற்றத்தைப் பார்ப்பது போலத் தன்னுடைய குற்றத்தையும் ஒருவனால் பார்க்க முடியுமானால், நிலைபெற்ற இந்த உயிருக்கு ஏதேனும் துன்பம் வருமா?
explanation: This couplet highlights the common human tendency to easily spot the flaws in others while ignoring one's own. It asks a rhetorical question: if a person develops the ability to examine their own faults as critically as they do a stranger's, could any evil befall them? The word 'காண்கிற்பின்' emphasizes the rare ability and effort required to truly see oneself. By turning the critical eye inward, a person avoids the harm that comes from ignorance and backbiting, ensuring a peaceful existence.
